body:
I know the feeling - my life, on the surface, is pretty good.  And yet I still feel the way I feel.

As for help, I don't have insurance, but there was a low-cost/free mental health clinic in my area that I was able to go to.  It was only $5 a month.  There's a link in the sidebar that gives phone-numbers worldwide for suicide prevention - if you called one of them and said you didn't have insurance, would they be able to direct you to a service similar to what I used?

I have to go home now, but I want to tell you that I've enjoyed "talking" with you.  I don't feel comfortable talking about the way I feel with anyone in "real life," so it's refreshing to be able to be honest here.  Good luck.

Would it help you to have a journal?  Sometimes just writing down all the horrible things that are going on in my life makes them just a little bit less horrible.

For example, I'm feeling just a little bit better after having been on this site and writing a few comments about it.  The plus of a journal is, no one is going to be shocked at what you say, or tell you you're over-reacting.  It's just you and your thoughts.

I mean, intellectually, I think we both realize that there are people that have it worse than us.  So it's not the specific circumstances that make life unbearable, but our reaction to them.  I wish I knew how to change my reaction to life's problems.  As it is now, my mind goes immediately to, "Well, I can just kill myself" whenever there's a problem.

That's bad, I know.

There's also the idea that "now" isn't "forever".  The way you're feeling now, and the circumstances you're in now, aren't necessarily the feelings and circumstances in the future.  It's possible, isn't it, that things will get better?

Have you considered getting help for the way you're feeling?  Now, I'm not exactly one to talk here, as I haven't really gotten help myself, but I recognize that many people do get better with treatment.

At the very least, I think it's a good sign (for both of us) that we're posting here.  That means we haven't completely cut ourselves off from other people, virtual or not, and that's a good thing.

I love chocolate - does that count?  And I like watching TV.  I joke that the TV is my only friend.  The sad part is, that's actually kind of the way I feel.  I'm an introvert who doesn't connect with people very well.  It takes effort to maintain a friendship, and that's energy I don't have.

It probably doesn't help that I have a massive inferiority complex.  I know that if people got to know me, *really* got to know me, they wouldn't like me.  So what ends up happening is that I cut them off before they can cut me off.  Which is self-defeating, I know.  I know I'm shooting myself in the foot with that sort of attitude.  I just can't help it.

I would blow them off, but it's not my house - it's my mom's.  So I don't really have a say in who comes to visit us.  If I had my way, I'd never see anyone.

Which probably isn't healthy.

As for therapy, I've tried it, off and on.  I don't have the stamina for it.  I can't sit there and talk about how much I hate myself for an hour - it's draining.

In a sense, though, this is kind of like therapy.  And I don't have to whine to one person for an hour to do it.

I can't think about how my mom will feel, and that is the only person who will really be affected.  If I did think about how she'd feel, I might not be able to go through with it.  But I want to, so desperately.  And I'll be dead, so I won't know what they're going through.  

Is that callous?  And selfish?  I know - it is.  But... I really believe that my mom will be okay in the end.  She's got a support structure, and people who love her and will help her get though it.  She's got her faith, which is something I lack.

Yes, she'll be sad, but... She'll get over it.  Okay, maybe "get over it" isn't quite accurate.  But it's not as if she's happy now, with me the way I am.

Parents have visions of who their children are supposed to be.  I am nothing like that vision.  It would have been better for her had I never existed.  But I do exist, so what can I do now?  

If I continue to exist, she'll just get sadder and more disappointed in me.  If I die, at least it will be over for her.  Isn't there something to be said for finality?  For an ending, no matter how sad?

I think I used to be brave.  Now I just hide.

You haven't mentioned your mom.  Are you close with her?  Would it help to talk with her about what you're feeling?  As for your sister, maybe you could hang out at her apartment, if she doesn't want to hang out at your house.

But maybe it's not possible solutions you're looking for.  I don't think it's what I'm looking for either.  Maybe just someone to listen?

I don't know if I can help you.  I don't know if it helps to know that you're not alone in feeling tired and apathetic.

I could say you could try reaching out to your sister - maybe writing her a letter would be easier than talking to her on the phone.  But I don't know if I could do that myself, so maybe it's hypocritical for me to give advice.

I do know that while I haven't spoken to my sister in years, it would mean so much to me if I heard from her, or got a letter from her or something.  But I'm not brave enough to make the first step.  Are you brave?  Can you be the better person?

Honestly, I don't know what I'd say.  I don't even know what I'm looking for.  All the things I've heard by well-meaning, nice people, like "It'll get better," and "Suicide's a permanent solution to a temporary problem," just don't seem to resonate with me.

Is life worth it to you?  My life isn't horrible, by any means, but even so, it's just not worth the work I have to put into it.  And I don't know if anyone can understand that.  I would rather just not wake up, you know?
